findings.title: No test for --git-* option wiring on bootstrap
findings.problem: No test checks that the bootstrap command registers --git-repo, --git-branch and --git-path or forwards them to runBootstrap. Bootstrap cases in analytics-sync-cli.test.ts only pass --webhook, --include-external and --lookback-days; the --git-repo help assertions are on `install`. Every run-bootstrap test calls runBootstrap directly with a hand-built options object. (regression-gap)
findings.impact: If an option is dropped or renamed, commander rejects the flag or runBootstrap receives undefined, and no test fails. The shipped git-only bootstrap flow would be dead from the CLI. Consumer: the `sync bootstrap` action in index.ts.
findings.recommendation: In analytics-sync-cli.test.ts, parse ['sync','bootstrap','--git-repo','git@h:o/r.git','--git-branch','main','--git-path','reports'] and assert runBootstrap received { gitRepo, gitBranch, gitPath }, plus a bootstrap.helpInformation() check for '--git-repo <url>', '--git-branch <name>' and '--git-path <dir>'
findings.check_notes: analytics-sync-cli.test.ts:200-210 asserts bootstrap forwards gitRepo/gitBranch/gitPath; help assertions at 123-128 cover the three options.

fix.change: Added bootstrap --git-* option forwarding and help tests
fix.test: analytics-sync-cli.test.ts: forwards --git-repo/--git-branch/--git-path; bootstrap --help lists git options

findings.title: Bootstrap help description omits git target
findings.problem: Story AC24 requires the bootstrap help text to describe choosing webhook, git or both. The command .description still reads 'connect a Teams channel and SharePoint folder, then print the install command...'; only the --git-* option help and a code comment changed. The unchanged analytics-sync-cli.test.ts:102-104 assertion pins the stale text.
findings.impact: `codemie analytics sync --help` tells leads bootstrap is Teams/SharePoint only; required criterion AC24 is only partly met, and the stale-fixture test would fail on any correction.
findings.recommendation: Update the .description to cover the git target and the three-way choice, update the doc comment above createSyncBootstrapCommand, and update the pinned expectation in analytics-sync-cli.test.ts so it reflects the new contract.
findings.check_notes: index.ts:103-105 description now names Teams webhook, git repository, or both; test pin at analytics-sync-cli.test.ts:102-104 updated to match.

fix.change: Bootstrap .description and doc comment now describe the webhook/git/both choice; pinned expectation updated

findings.title: Retained saved git URL shown as default unvalidated
findings.problem: In Change targets, adding git to a setup that holds a retained (git-off) URL returns { startId, state, onlyTarget } without discardStaleAnswers. checkReuse runs only on the kept targets, so git is skipped. stepGitRepo then passes current.gitRepoUrl to askGitDetails as the prompt default, which inquirer displays.
findings.impact: A hand-edited or otherwise credential-bearing saved gitRepoUrl can reach the terminal, contradicting AC10 and the security doc ('never stored or printed'). Reachability needs a tampered state file, so unconfirmed as a normal path.
findings.recommendation: In resolveChangeTargets, re-validate retained git details (or run discardStaleAnswers) before running the added git step; in askGitDetails, do not offer a saved default that fails validateGitRepoUrl.
findings.check_notes: guided-late-steps.ts unchanged, but git-step.ts askGitDetails now passes saved values through safeDefault (validate, drop on failure or blank), so a credential-bearing retained URL is never shown as a prompt default.

fix.change: askGitDetails offers a saved repo/branch/path as default only when it still validates
fix.test: guided.test.ts: Change targets over a retained credential-bearing git URL never offers it as default

findings.title: Target choice not persisted on fresh start
findings.problem: AC23 requires that interrupting after the target choice resumes at the first unanswered step for the chosen targets. resolveFreshStart returns { startId, state } for git-only and for the 'not imported' answer without calling saveBootstrapState, and stepTarget never saves. The first save happens only after a step answer.
findings.impact: An interrupt right after choosing targets leaves no state file, so the next run re-asks the target instead of resuming; a required story criterion is unmet.
findings.recommendation: Call saveBootstrapState with { version: 2, targets } immediately after stepTarget in resolveFreshStart, before returning on every path.
findings.check_notes: guided-start.ts resolveFreshStart calls saveBootstrapState({version:2,targets}) right after stepTarget, before every return path.

fix.change: resolveFreshStart saves {version:2,targets} right after the target choice
fix.test: guided.test.ts: saves the target choice right away (git-only and not-imported)

findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard broken by this change; blocks the workflow per standards review.
findings.recommendation: move the start-point resolution helpers (resolveFreshStart through resolveStartStep and their StartPoint type) into a sibling module such as guided-start.ts, as was done with guided-late-steps.ts.
findings.check_notes: start-point helpers moved to new guided-start.ts (256 lines); guided.ts now 305 lines.

findings.title: Blank --git-repo escapes as uncaught error
findings.problem: `--git-repo ""` (or whitespace) passes givesAnyTarget because the raw flag is defined, but validateGitSettings returns undefined for it. With no webhook either, no checks run and buildInstallCommand (outside the try) throws SyncConfigError. With --webhook plus a blank --git-repo the git flag is silently dropped.
findings.impact: runBootstrap is documented as never throwing and the commander action has no catch, so lead gets an unhandled rejection instead of a clean exit 1; no test covers it.
findings.recommendation: const hasTarget = hasAnyTarget(webhookUrl, git); if (!hasTarget) { deps.err('--git-repo is empty'); return 1; } and add a run-bootstrap test: runBootstrap({ gitRepo: '   ' }, deps) returns non-zero without throwing.
findings.check_notes: blank --git-repo routes to runNonInteractive; validateNonInteractive throws SyncConfigError '--git-repo is empty', caught, returns 1. No uncaught throw.

fix.change: Blank --git-repo throws a SyncConfigError during validation, giving a clean exit 1

findings.impact: Documented code-quality standard broken by this change.
findings.recommendation: extract the git-target handling (validation and test push) and the webhook-target handling into separate helper functions called from runNonInteractive.
findings.check_notes: runNonInteractive now ~21 lines; logic split into validateNonInteractive, runChecks, printNonInteractiveResult.

findings.title: No cleanup line when webhook sent but git failed
findings.problem: In non-interactive dual-target mode, if the webhook test passes and the git test fails, the Teams/SharePoint test file is already delivered. The failure path returns 1 without printing CLEANUP_LINE.
findings.impact: The lead is not told to delete the delivered test file, leaving a stray artifact in the team channel/folder.
findings.recommendation: When a webhook send fulfilled but another check rejected, print CLEANUP_LINE before returning 1.
findings.check_notes: runChecks returns webhookSent; runNonInteractive prints CLEANUP_LINE on failure when the webhook test file was delivered.

fix.change: Print CLEANUP_LINE when the webhook send succeeded but another check failed
fix.test: run-bootstrap.test.ts: cleanup line when webhook delivered but git failed; absent when webhook failed

findings.title: --git-branch/--git-path without --git-repo ignored
findings.problem: validateGitSettings returns undefined when no repo is set, so a valid --git-branch or --git-path passed without --git-repo is silently dropped. With --webhook plus --git-branch the lead gets a webhook-only command; on a TTY with no target flag the guided wizard starts.
findings.impact: Lead assumes the branch applied; non-interactive mode is meant to fail closed.
findings.check_notes: runBootstrap rejects --git-branch/--git-path without a non-blank --git-repo with exit 1 before any target routing.

fix.test: run-bootstrap.test.ts: branch/path without repo, with and without TTY

findings.title: v2 state shape check ignores targets contents
findings.problem: isBootstrapStateShape accepts any version 2 file whose targets is an object. targets {} , {webhook:false,git:false} or non-boolean values load fine; stepsFor then drops the target step and toInstallCommandOptions yields no target.
findings.impact: Step headings and [1] indexing misbehave, Start over lands on lookback, and Reuse reaches buildInstallCommand, which throws. Needs a hand-edited or corrupt file.
findings.check_notes: isBootstrapStateShape requires boolean webhook and git with at least one true for version 2.

fix.change: v2 state shape requires boolean webhook/git flags with at least one true
fix.test: state-store.test.ts: v2 file with empty/off/non-boolean targets is discarded with a notice

findings.title: Reuse revalidates only the git repo URL
findings.problem: REVALIDATORS['git-repo'] calls validateGitRepoUrl(state.gitRepoUrl) only: a blank URL passes (it returns undefined) and the saved gitBranch/gitPath go to the printed install command without validateGitBranch/validateGitPath.
findings.impact: A hand-edited or old state file can print --git-repo "" or an invalid/option-like branch or path into the shared command, which install later rejects. Reachability needs a tampered state file.
findings.recommendation: if (validateGitRepoUrl(s.gitRepoUrl) === undefined) throw new Error('missing'); validateGitBranch(s.gitBranch); validateGitPath(s.gitPath);
findings.check_notes: git-repo REVALIDATORS rejects a blank URL and runs validateGitBranch and validateGitPath on saved values.

fix.change: git-repo re-validator rejects a blank URL and validates saved branch and path
fix.test: state-store.test.ts: checkReuse resumes at git-repo for blank URL, bad branch, escaping path
